title: United States Loses Measles-Free Status as Cases and Deaths Rise
subtitle: Public health officials report a significant increase in infections and the first child deaths in decades.

summary.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status after outbreaks continued for over a year. Health experts report nearly 5,500 cases across 47 states and jurisdictions. Recent data confirms 10 deaths, including several infants. The loss of this status highlights a major challenge for the national healthcare system. Officials are now calling for better access to vaccines to reverse this trend.
summary.zh: 美國因麻疹疫情持續超過一年，已正式失去麻疹根除國的地位。衛生專家報告指出，在四十七個州與司法管轄區內，累計病例已接近五千五百例。最新數據證實已有十人死亡，其中包括數名嬰兒。失去此地位凸顯了美國醫療體系面臨的重大挑戰。官員目前正呼籲改善疫苗取得管道，以扭轉此一趨勢。

paragraphs.en: The United States has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated. This announcement comes after a series of outbreaks that have lasted for more than one year, marking a significant change in the nation's public health landscape. According to MedPage Today, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)—a group of experts that monitors disease transmission—determined that the same measles strain has been spreading within the country for over 12 months. This is the primary reason the U.S. no longer meets the requirements for elimination.
paragraphs.zh: 美國已正式失去麻疹根除國的地位。這項宣布是在一系列持續超過一年的疫情爆發後發布的，標誌著該國公共衛生環境的重大轉變。根據醫學新聞網站 MedPage Today 報導，負責監測疾病傳播的專家組織「泛美衛生組織 (Pan American Health Organization, PAHO)」認定，同一種麻疹病毒株已在美國境內持續傳播超過十二個月。這是美國不再符合根除標準的主要原因。

paragraphs.en: The situation has become increasingly serious as the number of infections continues to climb. Ars Technica reports that there are now nearly 5,500 cases across 47 states and jurisdictions. This figure is more than double the total number of cases recorded in 2025. While measles was once a disease that doctors only read about in textbooks, it is now a real threat in many communities. The human cost of these outbreaks is also growing, with the national death toll reaching 10. This includes at least four infants, with recent reports of deaths in Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著感染人數持續攀升，情況變得日益嚴峻。科技新聞網站 Ars Technica 報導指出，目前在四十七個州與司法管轄區內，累計病例已接近五千五百例。此數字是二〇二五年總病例數的兩倍以上。麻疹曾經是醫師僅能在教科書中讀到的疾病，如今卻已成為許多社區的真實威脅。這些疫情爆發所造成的人命損失也在增加，全國死亡人數已達十人。其中包括至少四名嬰兒，近期在賓夕法尼亞州、紐約州與威斯康辛州皆有死亡案例傳出。

paragraphs.en: Health officials have expressed deep concern over these numbers. For many of the affected states, these are the first measles-related deaths in decades. In Pennsylvania alone, the health department has reported seven deaths, while Wisconsin has reported two. These outbreaks are not just affecting the unvaccinated; they are also placing a heavy burden on the entire healthcare system. Experts noted that when measles spreads, it uses up limited resources like hospital beds and intensive care unit (ICU) space, which can impact the care available to all patients.
paragraphs.zh: 衛生官員對這些數據表達了深切的憂慮。對於許多受影響的州而言，這是數十年來首次出現與麻疹相關的死亡案例。僅在賓夕法尼亞州，衛生部門就通報了七起死亡案例，威斯康辛州則通報了兩起。這些疫情不僅影響未接種疫苗者，也對整個醫療體系造成沉重負擔。專家指出，當麻疹擴散時，會消耗病床與加護病房等有限的醫療資源，進而影響所有病患能獲得的照護品質。

paragraphs.en: Public health experts point to declining vaccination rates as the main cause of this crisis. The measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine is highly effective, but the number of children receiving it has dropped since the COVID-19 pandemic. According to MedPage Today, only 10 states currently meet the target of 95% vaccination coverage for children entering kindergarten. While some families choose not to vaccinate, many others face practical barriers. These include confusion about medical recommendations, insurance coverage issues, and difficulty finding a place to get the vaccine. These problems are reported most often by families with lower incomes.
paragraphs.zh: 公共衛生專家指出，疫苗接種率下降是這場危機的主因。麻疹、腮腺炎與德國麻疹混合疫苗（簡稱 MMR 疫苗）具有極高的保護力，但自新冠肺炎疫情以來，接種該疫苗的兒童人數已有所下降。根據 MedPage Today 報導，目前僅有十個州達到幼兒園入學兒童百分之九十五的疫苗覆蓋率目標。儘管有些家庭選擇不接種，但許多家庭面臨的是實際障礙，包括對醫療建議的困惑、保險給付問題，以及難以找到接種疫苗的地點。這些問題在低收入家庭中尤為常見。

paragraphs.en: Despite the current challenges, many experts believe the situation can be improved. Research shows that the majority of Americans still support childhood vaccination. Data indicates that over 80% of U.S. adults and 76% of parents believe the benefits of the MMR vaccine are greater than the risks. This trust exists across different political groups, with high levels of confidence reported by both Democrats and Republicans. Public health leaders suggest that the path to regaining elimination status involves making vaccines easier to access and more affordable for all families.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管面臨當前的挑戰，許多專家仍認為情況可以改善。研究顯示，大多數美國人仍支持兒童疫苗接種。數據指出，超過百分之八十的美國成年人與百分之七十六的家長認為，接種 MMR 疫苗的益處大於風險。這種信任感跨越了不同的政治立場，無論是民主黨人還是共和黨人，都展現出高度的信心。公共衛生領袖建議，重獲麻疹根除地位的途徑在於讓所有家庭能更輕鬆、更實惠地取得疫苗。

paragraphs.en: To address the crisis, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is focusing on education and community support. CDC director Erica Schwartz has stated that the agency plans to prioritize clear communication to help families understand the importance of immunization. By improving access and removing the logistical hurdles that prevent children from getting their shots, officials hope to stop the spread of the virus. While the loss of measles-free status is a major setback, the history of other countries shows that it is possible to achieve high immunity levels again through coordinated public health efforts.
paragraphs.zh: 為了解決這場危機，美國疾病管制與預防中心 (CDC) 正致力於教育與社區支援。CDC 主任艾瑞卡·史瓦茲 (Erica Schwartz) 表示，該機構計畫優先進行清晰的溝通，以協助家庭了解免疫接種的重要性。透過改善取得疫苗的管道並消除阻礙兒童接種的後勤障礙，官員們希望能遏止病毒傳播。雖然失去麻疹根除地位是一大挫折，但其他國家的歷史經驗顯示，透過協調一致的公共衛生努力，再次達成高免疫水準是有可能的。

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific reason the United States lost its measles-elimination status?

options.A: The national death toll has reached 10 people.
options.B: A single strain of the virus has been circulating in the country for more than a year.
options.C: Only 10 states currently meet the 95% vaccination coverage target.
options.D: The number of infections has nearly doubled compared to the year 2025.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，PAHO 認定同一種麻疹病毒株在境內持續傳播超過 12 個月，這是美國失去消除狀態的主要原因。選項 A 雖然是事實，但並非失去消除地位的定義因素。選項 C 是導致疫情的原因之一，而非判定失去資格的標準。選項 D 數據有誤，文中提到病例數是 2025 年的兩倍以上，而非僅僅是「幾乎翻倍」。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the impact of the measles outbreak on the broader healthcare system?

options.A: It has led to a shortage of medical professionals in rural areas.
options.B: It has caused hospitals to prioritize unvaccinated patients over others.
options.C: It creates a strain on resources that affects the quality of care for all patients.
options.D: It has forced the government to increase funding for intensive care units.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段，麻疹疫情會耗盡有限的資源（如病床與 ICU 空間），進而影響到所有病患的醫療照護。選項 A 文中並未提及。選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提到醫院會優先處理未接種疫苗者。選項 D 雖然聽起來合理，但文中並未提到政府因此增加了 ICU 的預算，這屬於過度推論。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, the author writes that the outbreaks are 'placing a heavy burden on the entire healthcare system.' What does 'burden' mean in this context?

options.A: A heavy physical load or weight.
options.B: A difficult situation that creates stress or demands on resources.
options.C: A medical condition that requires long-term treatment.
options.D: A legal responsibility to pay for damages.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此文中，burden 指的是對醫療系統造成的壓力與資源需求。選項 A 是該詞的字面意義（重量），在此不適用。選項 C 錯誤，burden 在此指代系統壓力，而非病患的病情。選項 D 雖然在法律語境下可能指責任，但在此處明顯是指醫療資源被佔用的負擔，而非賠償責任。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the measles crisis in the U.S.?

options.A: The U.S. healthcare system is fundamentally broken and cannot be fixed.
options.B: Most Americans are against vaccines, which is why the disease is spreading.
options.C: The loss of measles-free status is a serious issue, but it can be reversed through better access and education.
options.D: The recent measles outbreak is primarily the fault of lower-income families who refuse to get vaccinated.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章從疫情現況出發，分析了原因（疫苗接種率下降、取得困難），並在最後兩段強調多數民眾仍支持疫苗，且透過改善取得管道與教育，是有可能恢復消除狀態的。選項 A 過於悲觀且與文意不符。選項 B 與文中提到的「多數美國人支持疫苗」矛盾。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到低收入家庭面臨的是「實際障礙」，而非單純拒絕接種，且將責任歸咎於特定族群並非文章主旨。
